findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Align a66c's acceptance criteria with the parent non-negotiables (>=100-LOC floor, limit-file untouched, complexity ratchet new=0 increased=0, concern-boundary commit message, dual semantic+grep reference check).
evidence: a66c ACs are only: '<=700 lines', 'every name importable ... still importable', 'make lint and make typecheck exit 0'.

Parent 'Non-negotiable constraints on every child' include the >=100-LOC floor, 'Never raise the limit', complexity ratchet (via AC 'python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check reports new=0 increased=0'), 'commit message must NAME the concern boundary', and 'Both navigation tools' (Serena + grep).
Six sibling children each carry all of these as explicit ACs; a66c does not.
findings.finding: Child a66c-9329-e9c9-4aec uses a materially weaker acceptance-criteria template than its six siblings, omitting parent non-negotiable constraints: it does not assert the >=100-LOC floor for each new file, does not assert module-size-limit.txt is untouched, does not require the complexity ratchet to show no new/increased entries, does not require the commit message to name the concern boundary, and does not require dual semantic+grep reference verification.
scenarios: a66c lands a split that creates a sub-100-LOC shim, or raises complexity, or leaves a stale registry line-budget — none of which its own ACs would catch, unlike the six siblings.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-issue a66c using the same AC template as the six file-split children (or, if a66c is removed per the scope finding, this is moot).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit '<= 720 LOC (LIMIT - LIMIT/10)' target to each of the six file-split children so the parent's near-cap-band AC is measurable in the same terms.
evidence: Parent AC: 'Every one of the six in-scope files is at or below 720 LOC (the gate's own near-cap band, LIMIT - LIMIT/10), so none is left in the leading-indicator warning list.'
Every file-split child AC1: '... is under the cap with real headroom' — no number.
config child a66c names '<=700' but is out of the six-file scope, so it does not close this for any of the six.
findings.finding: Parent AC 'Every one of the six in-scope files is at or below 720 LOC (LIMIT - LIMIT/10 near-cap band)' is only PARTIALLY covered. No child AC states the 720 threshold; the six file-split children promise only 'under the cap with real headroom', which is the same direction but is not measurable in the same terms as the parent's specific numeric near-cap band.
findings.location: child 64ae-262f-990a-49ae; child 6f51-f8a4-b4fb-450c; child 8c3b-7479-e09d-465b; child e881-06e4-ffb2-4c4b; child ecf9-5e55-7386-4f04; child f97f-7161-7d10-4845
scenarios: A child lands its file at 740 LOC — 'under the cap with real headroom' as its AC reads, but still in the parent's 720-band warning list, so the parent AC fails the completion verifier.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend each file-split child's AC1 to read 'under 720 LOC (the near-cap band), verified by wc -l' rather than the qualitative 'real headroom'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to each split child an AC requiring any registry/allowlist/line-budget keyed to a moved symbol's OLD location to be updated in the same change.
evidence: Parent AC (second block): 'Any registry, allowlist or line-budget keyed to a moved symbol's OLD location is updated in the same change as the move (learned from Gerrit 1916, where a split left a stale seam line-budget and failed CI on the next run).'
Child ACs only cover: 'All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep' — reference set, not registry/allowlist/line-budget entries.
No child AC mentions 'line-budget', 'allowlist', or 'registry'.
findings.finding: Parent AC 'Any registry, allowlist or line-budget keyed to a moved symbol's OLD location is updated in the same change as the move (learned from Gerrit 1916)' is UNCOVERED. No child AC delivers this observable outcome. The children's 'All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep' covers code symbol references but not registries/allowlists/line-budgets keyed to the old file location — the exact artifact class the parent AC and the 1916 anecdote call out.
findings.location: child 64ae-262f-990a-49ae; child 6f51-f8a4-b4fb-450c; child 8c3b-7479-e09d-465b; child e881-06e4-ffb2-4c4b; child ecf9-5e55-7386-4f04; child f97f-7161-7d10-4845; child a66c-9329-e9c9-4aec
scenarios: A split moves a symbol out of a file that has a per-seam line-budget entry keyed to the old path; grep+Serena find no stale code reference, the child passes, and CI fails on the next run exactly as Gerrit 1916 did.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend each child's reference-verification AC to include: 'and any registry/allowlist/line-budget entry keyed to the old file path or symbol location is updated in the same commit.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Merge the two duplicated '## Acceptance Criteria' sections into one, keeping the precise 720-LOC threshold and folding in the unique registry/allowlist-update and child-close criteria.
evidence: First AC section: 'Every one of the six in-scope files is at or below 720 LOC'
Second AC section: 'under the 800-LOC cap with REAL headroom (not one or two lines), verified by wc -l'
Both sections separately restate: no file <100 LOC, module-size-limit byte-identical, commit names concern boundary, behaviour-preserving tests, lint/typecheck/complexity
findings.finding: The plan contains TWO separate '## Acceptance Criteria' sections whose contents overlap and partly diverge, creating a duplicate/near-duplicate requirement set.
findings.suggested_fix: Consolidate into a single Acceptance Criteria list: adopt '<=720 LOC' as the headroom definition (drop the vaguer 'not one or two lines' wording), and retain the second section's unique items (registry/allowlist keyed to old location updated in the same change) plus the first section's child-close criterion.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a single, measurable headroom target (recommend the concrete '<=720 LOC' band) and remove the subjective 'not one or two lines' phrasing so the pass/fail line is unambiguous.
evidence: 'Every one of the six in-scope files is at or below 720 LOC'
'under the 800-LOC cap with REAL headroom (not one or two lines)'
findings.finding: The two AC sections give two different headroom targets — a precise '<=720 LOC (LIMIT - LIMIT/10)' vs a subjective 'REAL headroom (not one or two lines)' — which is an unresolved conflicting signal about the required end-state.
findings.location: AC line 'at or below 720 LOC' vs AC line 'REAL headroom (not one or two lines)'
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the objective '<=720 LOC' as the sole headroom criterion; delete the 'REAL headroom (not one or two lines)' wording or reframe it as explanatory rationale for the 720 number.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Merge the two duplicated Acceptance Criteria blocks into one authoritative set and reconcile the headroom target (720 hard cap vs 'real headroom').
evidence: First block: 'Every one of the six in-scope files is at or below 720 LOC (the gate's own near-cap band).'
Second block: 'Each of the six target files is under the 800-LOC cap with REAL headroom (not one or two lines).'
findings.finding: The plan contains two separate 'Acceptance Criteria' headings with overlapping-but-differently-worded criteria (e.g. one requires <=720 LOC as a hard AC, the other only requires 'REAL headroom'). The end-state proof for the headroom goal is ambiguous.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the quantified <=720 LOC criterion as the single measurable proof and fold the qualitative 'real headroom' language into it as rationale.
